findings.explanation: Clinical note explicitly states 'brief assessment' for an acute upper respiratory tract infection (cough x 5 days, lungs clear, supportive care advised), but the claim bills 03.04A (comprehensive assessment). E/M billed (03.04A) within the 90-day global period following cholecystectomy (8 days post-op). Per SOMB GR 3.2.1, routine post-operative care is included in the surgical fee and should not be billed separately. The note describes routine post-op assessment (incision check, no infection, mild fatigue, discharged from surgical care) — this is included post-op care, not an unrelated service. Suggested fix: do not submit this claim to AHCIP. If the visit were for a genuinely unrelated condition, attach explanatory text to the claim — but do NOT recommend a -24 modifier, as Alberta has no such modifier.

The clinical note describes a brief telehealth follow-up for stable depression — single PHQ-9 score (6, down from 12), single medication continuation (sertraline 100mg), no side effects. The depth of this visit is consistent with a brief (03.01A) or minor (03.05A) assessment, not a comprehensive assessment. The claim bills 03.04A (comprehensive), which appears over-coded for the documented work. Recommend downgrading to 03.01A or 03.05A.

diagnosis_codes is empty while SOMB code 03.04A is billed. The note documents specific billable services (mammogram order, Pap smear, cardiovascular risk review, dietary counseling) that require a diagnostic indication on the claim. Per AHCIP rule A, an empty diagnosis_codes field with a SOMB code billed is the most-frequent auto-denial and fires regardless of the visit type.

The note is a routine 'Annual health maintenance visit' with no specific presenting complaint, complaint-directed history, or active problem being managed — only screening updates and lifestyle counseling. Alberta does not insure 'annual physical', 'health maintenance visit', 'wellness exam', 'preventive exam', or 'AWV' as separately billable SOMB services. This claim should not be submitted to AHCIP at all; the patient pays out-of-pocket or via private insurance.
